THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 11.08.2021 passed by the Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member, Prl.Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.6488/2018.

Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member, Prl.Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are as under; That on 30.09.2018 at about 06.30 a.m., the claimant was traveling in a Goods Mini Tempo bearing No.KA.11/B.5602 from Mysuru towards Malavalli on Malavalli-Mysuru road, when he reached near Banasiri Choultry, the driver of the said tempo drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and took it towards the extreme left side of the road and dashed against the wall of the bridge.
Due to the said impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Malavalli and then to Mandya, wherein, first aid treatment was given and thereafter, to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein, he has taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 12 days and underwent multiple surgeries and implants were inserted.

The claimant spent huge amount towards medical treatment,
food, nourishment and conveyance expenses.
NC: 2024:KHC:2162 3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy and was earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month by doing coolie work under respondent No.1 in his goods vehicle.

Due to the occurrence of accident and injuries suffered, the claimant is unable to do his work normally as he Mr Shekara Y D vs Mr Somaraju Y S on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185911595/
2 was doing prior to the occurrence of accident.

sentences.text: Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
3.2 On serve of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed ex parte.

Respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed statement objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed to the driver of the goods mini tempo.
However, it admitted that the insurance policy which is subject to the terms and conditions therein.
On the basis of pleadings, respondent-Insurance Company sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P14.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.15,07,900/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization and also held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimant with interest and respondent No.2 being the insurer shall indemnify respondent No.1 and pay the compensation amount within two months.
3.6
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation and it has not taken into consideration the avocation, age, income and magnitude of the injuries sustained by the claimant due to road traffic accident.

He further contends that under other heads also, the tribunal has awarded meager compensation, so also the tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of amenities,
future medical expenses and additional medical bills, which are part of the record before the tribunal.
It is also contended that the tribunal has awarded meager income towards loss of earning during laid up period.
Accordingly, he seeks to allow the appeal preferred by the claimant and seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel representing Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has not committed any error in awarding compensation.
He also contends that the claimant himself has admitted the income of NC: 2024:KHC:2162 Rs.12,000/-, which he was earning as on the date of occurrence of accident.
Hence, the question of enhancing of income does not arise.

He further contends that under other heads also, the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation,

3 which does not call for interference.

sentences.text: Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for both parties, it is not in dispute that accident occurred on 30.08.2018, while the claimant was traveling in goods mini tempo, the driver of the vehicle having lost control and dashed against the wall of the bridge and due to the accident, the claimant suffered grievous injuries.
Accordingly, he has suffered disability to an extent of 30%.

To establish the same,
the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P14, out of which, Exs.P1 to P3, P5, the Police records, which clearly disclose the laying of FIR and chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and Exs.P4, P6 to P14 are the medical records.

This clearly goes to show that the NC:
2024:KHC:2162 negligence has been rightly attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and the same does not call for interference.

7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the claimant, the tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.12,000/- per month, on the basis of admission made by the claimant himself as on the date of accident, the same requires to be taken in the present case.
The age of the claimant was 21 years at the time of the accident.
The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '18', which does not call for interference.
8. PW.2-Doctor has opined that the claimant sustained disability to the whole body at 31%.
The tribunal has assessed the disability to an extent of 30%, the same is retained and does not call for interference.
9. The tribunal has awarded Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it NC: 2024:KHC:2162 appropriate to award Rs.1,20,000/- as against the amount awarded by the tribunal.

10. Towards medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded Rs.6,09,300/-, whereas the tribunal has failed to award additional medical bills placed on record by the claimant before the tribunal to an extent of Rs.60,156/-, the same requires to be awarded under the head of medical expenses.
11. The tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards food, nourishment and attendant charges and Rs.2,000/- towards transportation charges.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under these heads.
12. Towards loss of future earnings due to disability, Rs.7,77,600/- is awarded by the tribunal, which does not call for interference as the same is just and reasonable.
13. Towards loss of income during laid up period, the tribunal has awarded Rs.24,000/-.

Considering the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:2162 magnitude of injuries suffered and avocation, the claimant would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.

14. The tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head loss of amenities.
Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under this head.
15. Towards future medical expenses, the tribunal has not awarded any amount.
PW.2-Doctor has opined that a sum of Rs.90,000/- is required for future medical expenses.
Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
